claims.text: The BMW 1 Series ‘F70’ is BMW’s fourth-generation 1 Series (new-model code F70) introduced for the 2024/2025 model years in Europe.

Professional reviews describe the facelifted Volkswagen Golf (Mk8.5 / 2024–2025) as having ‘rounded’ driving manners and, with adaptive dampers, a comfortable ride — but note the ride can feel firmer and noisy on larger wheels or poor surfaces.
claims.about: Volkswagen Golf driving and ride comfort (Mk8.5)

claims.text: UK reviews (Auto Express) say the Mk8.5 Golf is a comfortable and pleasant place to be overall but that ride quality is compromised on poorer surfaces and that larger wheels increase road noise and harshness.
claims.about: Volkswagen Golf ride quality and noise

claims.text: Journalists and owners have reported that the Golf’s drivetrain character (small TSI engines plus DSG/dually systems) can feel less engaging or ‘dull’ in real-world use, with some owners describing sluggish or uninvolving acceleration in non-performance trims.
claims.about: Golf drivetrain engagement and acceleration feel

claims.text: VW’s 1.5-litre petrol options for the Mk8/8.5 are offered in ~115 PS and ~150 PS states; the base 1.5 variants and their official 0–100 km/h performance (sub-10 s for stronger versions, slower for the lower-output units) help explain why some drivers find the base cars underpowered for spirited driving.
claims.about: VW Golf engine options and performance

claims.text: At the same time, German press testing of the Golf 1.5 eTSI notes software/hardware changes (e.g., starter-generator in mild-hybrid eTSI) that reduce some DSG ‘ruckle’/hesitation symptoms in those variants.
claims.about: Golf 1.5 eTSI transmission behaviour and DSG ruckling

claims.text: Mainstream European reviewers describe the BMW 1 Series (F70) as retaining a driver-focused character with generally better handling engagement than mainstream rivals, while advising that ride comfort depends strongly on trim and wheel/tire choice (standard Sport trim is more comfortable than optional M Sport or larger-wheel specifications).
claims.about: BMW 1 Series F70 handling vs ride comfort

claims.text: Several buyer’s guides and reviews (Carbuyer / CarGurus / CarUnited) state the F70 1 Series achieves an ‘excellent balance between sporty handling and ride comfort’ for many buyers, but they repeatedly caution that M Sport/large wheels or run-flat/performance tyres will make the ride noticeably firmer.

In drivetrain terms, the regular BMW 120 (F70) is offered with a ~170 hp petrol variant and uses a seven‑speed dual‑clutch automatic in most markets; that higher base output vs. the Golf’s lowest-output 115–150 hp options explains why some reviewers/owners find the BMW’s on-paper performance and overtake ability stronger than base Golfs.
claims.about: BMW 1 Series powertrain and gearbox information

claims.text: Owner and forum reports collected since 2024‑2026 back the customer comment that some Golf trims feel ‘underpowered’ or ‘sluggish’ in everyday driving and that some drivers dislike the transmission/DSG character; those criticisms appear concentrated on lower-output Golf variants and certain gearbox calibrations rather than on all Golf powertrain options.
claims.about: Owner reports of Golf feeling dull/sluggish and transmission complaints
